chung.Syllabus Name: Crisis Communications Management_Quản trị truyền thông khủng hoảng
chung.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
chung.Pre-Requisite: CCO201 or MKT304 or IMC301c or IMC301
chung.Description:
This course covers crisis communication theory, crisis management approaches, classic cases and the influence of culture on crisis communication. This course will introduce the definitions of crisis and how they come about, the importance of the Enterprise Risk Management framework in crisis prevention and preparation, and how we can recognise and address crises in case they happen. This course focuses on the role of communications throughout the crisis management process, as well as how to utilise media relations and social media to prevent and/or respond to crises.

Apart from learning academic theories, students will have opportunities to apply their acquired knowledge & skills in analysing a real-world case study, as well as developing a industry-facing crisis communication plan for an organisation ("client") and self-organising an accompanied simulated media conference to address a crisis of that organisation. Throughout that, students will be equipped with practical experience and skills to be ready for their future career path in the communications field.

Finally, students can also use AI to assist their practices and assignemnts.

danhGia: Test the acquainted knowledge which student obtained in the delivered chapters (Chapter 1, 6, 7, 8)

Individual Assessment (At home)
Type: Essay
Weight: 15%
Length: 1,500-2,000 words
Task Description:
Choose from the list of crisis case studies provided by the lecturer before and analyse one organisational crisis.
Your essay will include an overview of the crisis, a description of the organisation, a crisis timeline, actions and responses taken, a media analysis, stakeholder impacts, lessons learned, recommendations, and use appropriate matrix/models.
The essay should address the criteria as outlined in the assessment task and rubric mentioned during the class.
Students should use a mix of scholarly references, media coverage and organisational materials, as well as applying AI-tools to collect information and analyze the chosen crisis.

The whole class is divided into groups. Each group is assigned to make one crisis communication plan
Test the acquainted knowledge and skills which student obtained in the delivered chapters (Chapter 1-8, with an emphasis on Chapter 2-5)

Group Assessment
Type: Crisis Communication Plan (At Home) + Presentation (In the class)
Weight: 25%
Task Description:
Students working within a small group setting of 4-6 students to select one organisation in Vietnam, which must be accepted by the lecturer, then propose a crisis communication plan for that organisation. The plan must showcase all knowledge the students have gained in the class, and be delivered as a final report to their chosen organisation.
AI Application: Students have to demonstrate their capability of applying AI tool (ChatGPT, Claude.ai, etc...) in preparing templates in the crisis communication plan, which include (but aren't limited to) prewritten news release(s) and media alert.

Presentation: For the 15-minute presentation, each group have to showcase all of your key points mentioned in your report in front of your classmates.

Notes:
The detailed structure of a crisis communication plan could be found in the textbook (Chapter 5)
Further details of the crisis communication plan will be provided in class. The detailed marking criteria for this assessment will be provided to you by your lecturer.
The mark will be given based on each student's performance, not on the whole group's. It means each student will get their own mark.
The whole class is divided into groups. Each group is assigned to create one simulated media conference.
Test the acquainted knowledge and skills which student obtained in the delivered chapters (Chapter 4-7)

Group Assessment
Type: Simulated Media Conference (In the class)
Weight: 20%

Based on your crisis communication plan, each group will prepare for a media conference based on the scenario which will respond to a simulated crisis of your chosen organisation. Your media statement should be no more than 15 minutes in total and will be followed by a 15-minute Q&A from the “journalist” members of the class.
Before the media conference, your group have to prepare:
1. a media alert
2. a media kit, including the press release (to be delivered at the conference)
3. a one-page summary of key message
AI Application: Students have to demonstrate their capability of applying AI tool (ChatGPT, Claude.ai, etc...) in preparing the above-mentioned documents.

Notes:
Further details of the media conference will be provided in class. The detailed marking criteria for this assessment will be provided to you by your lecturer.
The mark will be given based on each student's performance, not on the whole group's. It means each student will get their own mark.
The questions will cover the lectures, class discussions, activities, exercises, and textbook.
